result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 3 FOUND, 2 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Reviewed all handwritten source, service/desktop configuration, compose files, Dockerfile, transforms and publish profile in eShopModernizedNTier. Credential evidence is location-only and [MASKED]. No explicit insecure ACL assignment or hard-coded cryptographic key confirmed. Runtime identity, external permissions and external logging configuration were not available. Generated/test/temp/dependency code excluded; static review only.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: The SQL Server deployment contains a literal administrator password [MASKED] in sql.data.environment.SA_PASSWORD (eShopModernizedNTier\docker-compose.override.yml:13). The healthcheck also embeds that password [MASKED] for sqlcmd authentication (line 18). These are active deployment values rather than placeholders or comments; no secret values are reproduced.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem (eShopModernizedNTier\src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:65-71) accepts a remote catalog creation request and persists it with SaveChanges without recording an audit event, caller identity or affected record. The exposed operation is declared at eShopModernizedNTier\src\eShopWCFService\ICatalogService.cs:27-28. Full handwritten source and service configuration contain no application audit logger or interceptor for this security-relevant catalog mutation. Host access logs, if any, are not evidence of record-level auditing.
